why: The cloned repo contains the complete, modern (Python >=3.9) implementation of everything C2 needs: all five delta methods including the O(n) margin estimator (ternary_tree/delta_methods.py), the probabilistic-routing tree (ternary_tree/binary_ternary_tree.py), the O(n log n) splitter, decided/undecided metrics, an OpenML-CC18/medical data loader with a per-dataset checkpointing runner (benchmark/run_extended_benchmark.py), and the paper-table generator (benchmark/report_paper.py). Nothing must be reimplemented or ported: the only absent artifacts are the raw OpenML downloads (credit-g is OpenML dataset 31, ~1k x 20) and the results CSVs, and both are regenerated by the released code. The match target is a single small dataset at max_depth=4 with 5 folds, so the authors' entrypoint can be pointed at credit-g and run essentially as released.
entrypoints: python benchmark/run_extended_benchmark.py --collection cc18 --output results_cc18.csv   (restrict to credit-g via the dataset filter / a short driver that calls make_classifier(delta_method='margin', routing_method='probabilistic', max_depth=4) with 5-fold stratified CV and per-fold StandardScaler)
python benchmark/run_extended_benchmark.py --collection medical --output results_medical.csv   (secondary checks: diabetes C7, mammography C5)
python benchmark/report_paper.py --cc18 results_cc18_repaired.csv --breiman results_breiman.csv --medical results_medical.csv --output paper_tables.txt
pytest tests/ -v   (67 unit tests as a sanity gate on the delta methods and routing)
missing_artifacts: No precomputed results CSVs are shipped (results_cc18.csv, results_breiman.csv, results_medical.csv); they are produced by the runner.

README references results_cc18_repaired.csv — the repair step/notebook that produced it is not in the repo, so the CC18 path may need a small fix or a fresh run (irrelevant for the credit-g target, which uses the library directly).
OpenML data itself is not vendored: credit-g (dataset 31) must be downloaded at run time.
No trained models/weights — not needed, the trees are fit in-process in seconds.
blockers_seen: Network dependency on the OpenML server (openml>=0.14): installable on Python 3.12 but server latency/outage can stall the download; mitigated by caching after the first get_dataset call.
No GPU on this machine — irrelevant, the code is pure numpy/scikit-learn CPU.
15.4 GB RAM against the paper's 32 GB — irrelevant at this scale (N=1,000, d=20, depth 4).
docs point at an unreleased 'repaired' CC18 CSV, so the full 71-dataset sweep (C1/C3, ~3-4 h) would exceed this machine's 20-minute budget; the pinned target C2 does not.

feasibility.est_runtime_on_this_machine: ~5-15 minutes wall clock: 1-2 min editable install of numpy/scipy/scikit-learn/pandas/openml, <1 min to fetch credit-g (898 KB) and cache it, <10 s for the 5-fold depth-4 margin run, seconds for the clean re-run. Optional extras (diabetes C7 <1 min, mammography C5 1-3 min) still leave the run inside the 20-minute budget; the 71-dataset CC18 sweep for C1/C3 would not.

compute.basis: The match target is one N=1,000 / d=20 table, five folds, depth-4 trees, with a zero-hyperparameter O(n)-per-node margin delta — a few seconds of fitting — so the 15 minutes is dominated by pip install of numpy/scipy/scikit-learn/pandas/openml and the OpenML download plus a clean re-run.
